headline: Prices for homes in Vaughan are lower than a year ago. A typical home cost $1,106,600 in October, down 5.5%. Builders are still planning many towers in the VMC, and Vaughan has cut its building fees to help projects start.

status.label: Few starts, many plans
status.explanation: Vaughan has 3,144 homes under construction, down from 3,588 a year ago. Yet 89 development applications are active, including about 17,363 units in site plans.

status.label: Fewer buyers, cooler market
status.explanation: Vaughan had 263 resale sales in October, with 4.8 months of inventory. Fewer immigrants and students are arriving, which can mean fewer renters and buyers.

status.label: Prices down about 6%
status.explanation: The typical Vaughan condo apartment cost $504,900 in October, down 6.5% from a year ago. That is far below the March 2022 peak of $864,400. These prices cover all of Vaughan, not just the VMC.

status.label: Rents flat to slightly lower
status.explanation: Average rent in the wider Richmond Hill/Vaughan/King zone was $1,726 in 2025, down from $1,762 in 2024. Vacancy was 2.4%. This zone is bigger than the VMC.

status.label: Big plans, cautious building
status.explanation: Vaughan approved a master plan for 17 mixed-use towers on the Toromont site. Meanwhile, the VMC tract saw 673 starts so far in 2026, well below 3,380 in 2021.

personas.bottom_line: Prices have come down, but rates are still high, so monthly costs matter as much as price.

points.text: A typical Vaughan condo apartment is $504,900, about $40,000 lower than a year ago.
The posted 5-year mortgage rate is 6.19%. Posted rates are usually higher than rates people actually get.
There are 419 condo apartments listed for sale, so buyers have choices.
Prices could keep drifting lower, which works against anyone who buys now.

watch: Bank of Canada decision on December 9, 2026

personas.bottom_line: Rents in the wider area are roughly flat, and new buildings may add choice.

points.text: Average rent in the zone was $1,726 in 2025, compared with $1,917 in the Toronto CMA.
Vaughan finished 6,368 homes in 2025, which adds rental and ownership options.

personas.bottom_line: Townhouses and detached homes are cheaper than a year ago, but still costly.

points.text: A typical townhouse costs $714,500, down 8.9% in a year.
A typical detached home costs $1,482,000, down 5.4%.

personas.bottom_line: Sellers face a market where prices are lower and homes take more effort to sell.

points.text: Homes sold for about 97% of the asking price in October.
The typical Vaughan home is worth about $480,000 less than at the March 2022 peak.
New condo supply nearby adds competition for resale condos.

personas.bottom_line: Lower prices and flat rents mean returns are not guaranteed, and risks are real.

points.text: Condo apartment prices are down 6.5% in a year while rents are flat to lower in the wider zone.
Many projects are planned, so competition from new condos could grow.

personas.bottom_line: Selling a larger home and buying a condo both happen in a softer market.

points.text: Detached homes are down 5.4% and condo apartments are down 6.5%, so both sides of a move are cheaper.

watch: Price gap between detached homes and condos

scenarios.name: optimistic
scenarios.summary: Rates ease, buyers return, and prices stabilize or rise.

assumptions.assumption: Rate falls below its current 2.5% level over the next two years.

drivers.text: Many planned towers show builder interest.

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.summary: Prices stay soft or drift lower, and building stays modest.

assumptions.assumption: Rate stays near 2.5%, with the next decision on December 9, 2026.
Vaughan starts stay between about 800 and 3,800 units over the next 12 months, as in the baseline.

scenarios.name: pessimistic
scenarios.summary: Weak jobs and high rates push prices lower and delay projects.

assumptions.assumption: Vaughan condo apartment benchmark falls toward the low end of the baseline band, near $400,000 by October 2027.

baseline_views.reason: Prices are trending down but not sharply; I see no strong evidence to depart from the baseline.
Falling prices, high mortgage rates and weak jobs offset lower building fees; in line.
Condo prices fell 6.5% in a year; no strong evidence to change the baseline.
Weak demand from fewer newcomers is balanced by lower prices; in line.
Fee cuts may help starts, but trends are weak; in line with a wide band.
Past starts swing widely, so I keep the baseline view.
Completions of towers like Festival may reduce the total while new starts add to it; in line.
Rents fell slightly in 2025 and vacancy is 2.4%; in line, toward the lower half of the band.
